rules: Import `ruststream_amqp::prelude::*` at a mount site and name the policy `Publish` there; a handler body imports `ruststream::prelude::*` and bounds a slot with a capability such as `Out<impl Publisher>` (Components > AMQP broker > Prelude).

Describe a subscription with `AmqpAddress::queue(name)` for competing consumers or `AmqpAddress::topic(name)` for a copy each; keep `AmqpAddress::raw` and a bare `#[subscriber("name")]` for a broker's own address syntax (Components > Subscriptions).
Mount a handler written without the macros as `subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue(..), Body)`, the descriptor passed as the source as it is (Components > Subscriptions).

Set the link credit with `.credit(nonzero!(n))` on the descriptor; it is the window the broker may send ahead, refilled once half of it is settled, so more than `n` deliveries can be unsettled (Components > Subscriptions > credit).

Settle through the handler's outcome: `ack()` sends `accepted`, `retry()` sends `modified` with `delivery-failed` so the broker counts the attempt, and `drop()` sends `rejected` (Components > Dispositions).

Read a subscription at most once with `.settle(Settle::AtMostOnce)` only where a lost message costs less than a repeated one; its `ack` and `nack` report `AckError::Unsupported` (Components > Dispositions > Settle).

Cap redeliveries with `.max_attempts(n).dead_letter(address)` after `include`; a `retry_after(delay)` copy goes back to the subscription's own address, and `.out_retry(Publish).transform(..)` marks the copies (Guides > Retries and dead letters).

Take a batch with a slice handler and `.batch(n)` at the mount site; the client assembles it, and `.batch_wait(duration)` on the descriptor closes a partial one (Components > Subscriptions > Batches).

Publish through `Publish` at the mount site (`.out_reply(Publish)`, `.out(marker, Publish).build()`); a publish the broker does not accept fails with `AmqpError::PublishNotAccepted` (Components > Publish).

Ask with `request(msg, timeout)` on a slot bound `Out<impl RequestReply>`, and answer from a responder through an `Out<impl Publisher>` slot with `.to(reply_to)`, echoing `correlation-id` (Components > Request-reply).

Publish several messages together or not at all through `TransactionalPublish` (feature `transaction`) and a slot bound `Out<impl TransactionalPublisher>`, with `begin_transaction`, `commit` and `abort` (Guides > Transactions).

Under `workers(n)`, bind the slot `Out<impl OwnedTransactions>` and open a transaction per delivery with `owned_transaction()`; the workers share one publisher, so `begin_transaction` serves one delivery at a time (Components > Transactions).

Test the production app: hand the app `main` runs to `TestApp::start` with the `testing` feature, address the broker as `tb.broker::<AmqpBroker>()`, and run the same body on `TestApp::start_live` for credit and dead-letter policy (Components > Testing).

Configure the login with `AmqpBroker::sasl(Sasl::plain(user, password))` for credentials from the environment, and enable `rustls` or `native-tls` for an `amqps://` URL on a host name or an IPv4 address (Guides > Connecting to production).
